title: Requirement Steward multi-agent function deliberation
observed_problem: docs/CURRENT_STATE.json identifies requirement_steward_multi_agent_function_deliberation as the only canonical open work item. Current-main discovery found no existing canonical RequirementSteward symbol. DOR already contains the adjacent primitives that must constrain any solution: provider-neutral Council deliberation and routing; immutable/fingerprinted Council role definitions, stage templates and allocation pools; durable Council session provenance bound to organization/context/revisions; formal dispute/dissent representation; the canonical Agent Registry; the general orchestrator boundary; and Governance v0 distinct-role routing. What is not represented as a verified canonical boundary is a Requirement Steward capability that takes one exact identified requirement/problem question, obtains bounded multi-agent perspectives through the existing deliberation machinery, preserves the provenance and disagreement behind those perspectives, and emits a non-authoritative advisory artifact that downstream governance/design can inspect.
impact: Without a canonical boundary, cross-functional requirement interpretation can become ad hoc or single-agent, provenance for perspectives can be lost, dissent can be flattened into an opaque synthesis, and downstream design/governance can receive an interpretation that is difficult to bind back to the exact input and deliberation evidence.
affected_concepts: Agent Registry identity and capability declarations
Development Governance v0 role separation and routing
constraints: Reuse the canonical Council provider-neutral deliberation primitives and canonical Agent Registry; do not create a parallel agent/provider stack.
Do not create a second scheduler, Authority engine, GovernanceCoordinator, or generic orchestration system.
Requirement deliberation is advisory/evidence-producing only. It must not authorize, approve scope, mutate project state, or execute work.
Preserve exact immutable input identity and the Council configuration/provider-binding identities used for the run.
Preserve role/provider attribution, evidence references, and material dissent/disputes; synthesis must not erase disagreement provenance.
Artifact identity must bind its captured immutable contents; do not assume stochastic model runs produce identical outputs from identical prompts.
Missing, invalid, disabled, or incompatible role/provider bindings must fail closed through existing allocation/routing rules.
Preserve Governance v0 separation between Product Owner, Orchestrator, Coder, Auditor and Independent Reviewer.
Human Owner must not become a routine prompt router for deliberation roles.

Reuse existing durable Council/session persistence where it satisfies the approved design. If new durable meaning or schema is required, design must return through the semantic gate before adding persistence/migrations.
Preserve organization/project/context binding wherever the source requirement already carries those identities.
non_goals: no automatic requirement approval or scope mutation
no replacement of Product Owner, GovernanceCoordinator, Auditor or Independent Reviewer
no second generic orchestrator or scheduler
no database migration in v1 unless a later approved design proves it necessary and explicitly gates it
proposed_scope: Define a Requirement Steward application/service boundary that, using existing canonical primitives where possible, accepts one immutable, identified requirement/problem/function question plus bounded context/evidence references.
Resolve a bounded, approved Council role/template/allocation configuration rather than inventing agents at runtime.
Run provider-neutral Council deliberation with frozen provenance bindings.
Preserve attributable turns, evidence references and material disputes/dissent.
Expose a content-addressed advisory deliberation result (reusing/extending an existing Council artifact if sufficient, introducing only the minimum wrapper if design proves one is required).
Bind downstream consumption to the exact input and deliberation provenance.
Have no Authority or Execution capability and cannot mutate approved scope.
